extra.message: The pageId value, sourced from the /dashboard/<pageId> route parameter, is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to db.execute() ('SELECT pageId, title, content FROM pages WHERE pageId='+pageId) instead of being parameterized. This allows SQL injection against the SQLite database.

request.url (attacker-controlled via the requested path) is interpolated into a template string with .format(request.url) and the result is passed to render_template_string(). An attacker can request a URL containing Jinja2 syntax (e.g. /{{7*7}}) which is evaluated server-side, resulting in Server-Side Template Injection / arbitrary code execution. The globally-exposed system_call context processor (os.popen) makes this directly exploitable as RCE.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The /about/sync endpoint reads attacker-supplied hex data from request.form['data_obj'], converts it via bytes.fromhex, writes it to pickle.hacker, and then calls pickle.load() on it. Because pickle deserialization executes arbitrary code defined by the pickle payload, this allows remote code execution.

User input from the /information/<input> URL parameter is base64-decoded and passed to yaml.load() without specifying a SafeLoader. PyYAML's default/full loader permits construction of arbitrary Python objects via tags such as !!python/object/apply, enabling remote code execution.

User-supplied XML from request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString(), which is backed by expat and resolves external entities by default. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, including disclosure of local files and SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The /validator/getXML endpoint takes fileName directly from request.form['example_file'] and uses it in open(fileName) and send_file(fileName) without any path validation. An attacker can supply absolute paths or ../ sequences to read and download arbitrary files from the server (e.g. /etc/passwd).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: In the /validator/uploads endpoint the uploaded file's filename (file.filename, fully attacker-controlled) is concatenated into the save path as 'uploads/'+filename with no sanitization of path separators. The allowed_file() check only validates the extension, so a name like ../../shell.html passes and allows writing files to arbitrary locations on disk.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: A context processor exposes a system_call(command) helper that runs os.popen(command).read() and is injected into the Jinja2 template context of every rendered template. Because the argument is executed by the shell without sanitization and the function is reachable from user-controlled template input (e.g. via the SSTI in the 404 handler), this enables arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: User input from request.form.get('search') is passed to the search template, which renders it with {% autoescape false %}{{search}}{% endautoescape %}. The response also explicitly disables the browser XSS filter via X-XSS-Protection: 0 (line 11). This allows reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The user-supplied message link (item[3], stored through /messaging/new) is rendered inside an href attribute as <a href="{{item[3]}}">. Jinja2 HTML autoescaping does not neutralize javascript: URLs, so a stored value such as javascript:alert(document.cookie) executes script when a victim clicks the link, resulting in stored cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /webmaster route unconditionally sets session['loggedin'] = random for every visitor without performing any authentication. Because the protected /confidential endpoint (and the layout's gated menu) rely solely on the presence of session['loggedin'], any unauthenticated user can visit /webmaster and then access /confidential, bypassing login entirely.

The /confidential endpoint guards sensitive salary data only with if(session['loggedin']):, which raises an unhandled KeyError for unauthenticated users and lacks any proper denial/redirect. Combined with other routes (e.g. /webmaster) that set session['loggedin'] without authentication, this authorization check is broken and the confidential data is exposed to unauthorized users.

CORS is configured with resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}, allowing every origin to make cross-origin requests to all routes. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials being set to true on the /confidential endpoint, this permits any malicious site to read authenticated responses from the application (CORS misconfiguration).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The /confidential response explicitly sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true while the application's global CORS policy allows all origins (runserver.py). This credentialed cross-origin access to a sensitive, session-protected endpoint allows malicious origins to read the confidential data of authenticated users.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY (used to sign session cookies) is hardcoded as the literal string 'random'. An attacker who knows this value can forge valid session cookies, including setting session['loggedin'] to bypass authentication on protected endpoints such as /confidential.

Flask debug mode is enabled (app.debug = True) and the server is bound to 0.0.0.0 (runserver.py). In production this exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger, leaking detailed stack traces/source and potentially enabling remote code execution through the debugger console, as well as disclosing sensitive application internals on errors.

Authentication is performed by comparing request values directly against the hardcoded credentials if(password == "admin" and username == "admin"). The application's valid credentials are embedded in source code, allowing anyone with source access to log in, and the check ignores the user database entirely.
